This document will describe the investigation carried out on the disposal of the solvent. Along with the solvent, the disposal investigation of solid spent catalyst used in the water gas shift reactor is explained in this attachment. 2.0 Solvent Disposal Investigation The solvent is not usually disposed of in day-to-day operations. However, solvent contamination is possible due to heat-stable salts (HSS) formation during the reaction, which can lead to Electrodialysis Reclaimer (EDR) waste and solvent disposal. The solvent handling system, including removal, has been described below. The solvent handling system has two subsystems. • Solvent Circulation Module • Solvent Maintenance Module 2.1 Solvent Disposal Investigation The Solvent Circulation Module (SCM) consists of the components necessary for transporting and efficiently utilizing the solvent in the carbon capture process. Transportation and control of the solvent require coordination of equipment in the Absorber (ABS), Stripper (STR), and Solvent Heat Exchanger (LRX) subsystems. The SCM primarily consists of the circulation equipment between the Absorber and Stripper. The cold-rich Solvent Pump moves the cold-rich solvent from the Absorber Sump to the Stripper. Most of the rich solvent passes through the LRX for heat recovery from the lean solvent.
